sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?composer 
 WHERE {
 ?composer rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?composer foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:composed_by ?composer .
 }
gold_question: Did this composer write the given tune?

review.note: Given the composer name and the tune object, find the composer object. The previous one would return all composer objects whereas this one differentiates by name so should hopefully return one or none. The question is not about who, we already have the name, rather it is about whether the composer is associated with the tune.

model_output.nl_question: Who is the composer with the given name who composed a musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL filters a MusicArtist by the given name and requires that they have composed a MusicalWork, returning that composer entity. No provided evidence aligns with the composer intent, so the question is generated from the query structure.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?arranger 
 WHERE {
 ?arranger rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?arranger foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:arranged_by ?arranger .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one arranger with this name in the graph?

review.note: This could be name disambiguation on the one hand - is there more than one arranger with this name in the dataset. Or, on the other hand, it could be a check whether there is an arranger with this name (this is what was generated), or whether this musician did any arrangements. The presence of 'distinct' suggests the former I would say.

model_output.nl_question: Which musician with the given name arranged at least one musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence mentions arrangers or arrangements, so the question is generated from the SPARQL itself. The query clearly selects the musician entity with a given name who is linked as arranger of a musical work, making the generated question a good fit despite lack of direct evidence.

PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>

 WHERE {
 ?band rdf:type mo:MusicGroup .
 ?band foaf:name "%s" .
 }
gold_question: Find the band by its name

model_output.nl_question: Which band has the given name?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence directly covers looking up a band by its name. The SPARQL clearly selects a MusicGroup whose foaf:name matches a given string, and the question reflects that intent.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT ?trackt ?signal
 WHERE {
 ?track rdf:type mo:Track .
 ?track dc:title ?trackt .
 ?track mo:track_number "%i" .
 ?medium mo:track ?track .
 ?medium dc:title ?mediumt .
 ?medium mo:record_number "%i" .
 ?release mo:record ?medium .
 ?release dc:title "%s" .
 ?signal mo:published_as ?track .
 }
gold_question: Given the album title, disk number and track number, find the track title and the associated signal

review.note: My main concern here is the album vs release difference - in NL we would talk about album title rather than release title; in the ontology, release was chosen rather than album to indicate the relation to time

model_output.nl_question: For the given release title, record number, and track number, what is the track’s title and the associated audio signal?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence directly matches the query’s intent. The question is derived from the SPARQL, which clearly filters by a release title, a record number, and a track number and returns the track title and its audio signal via mo:published_as.

sparql:
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?musician 
## WHERE {
## ?session mo:performer <%s> .
## ?session event:sub_event ?performance .
## ?performance mo:performer ?performer .
## ?performer dtl:musician ?musician .
## }
gold_question: Which musicians performed together with the given performer?

review.note: Missing context - the Jazz Ontology models all performances as part of a session, therefore this query is for all musicians who ever performed together with the given one

model_output.nl_question: Which musicians performed in the same session as the given performer?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL selects musicians from performances that are sub-events of a session featuring a given performer, effectively asking for the lineup in that session. The retained CQ about band line-up for a performance is thematically aligned but not session-scoped, so the match is partial.

retained_evidence_phrases.text: What is the band line-up for the given performance?

gold_question: List all places in the graph with their coordinates

review.note: The generated phrase is factually accurate but highly improbable in NL.

model_output.nl_question: Which places have latitude and longitude coordinates?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL clearly retrieves all locations (mtp:Location) that have both latitude and longitude, returning their labels. The only aligned evidence is a minimal query comment indicating the 'PLACES' section, so the question is primarily generated from the query semantics.

model_output.confidence_rationale: No textual evidence is provided. The SPARQL clearly selects all instances of organ:Organ and their rdfs:label, so asking for the names of all organs directly matches the query intent.

model_output.confidence_rationale: No natural-language evidence is provided, but the SPARQL clearly selects rdfs:label values for three specified organ entities. The question concisely reflects this intent without exposing opaque IDs.

gold_question: Which of the listed organs have an external website?
